prompt:
Image 1 is a flat lay of a Baseball kit, photographed from the front.

Photograph THAT SAME KIT from the BACK — the same garments, turned over:
- the shirt, laid flat and face DOWN, so its back is what you see
- the shorts below it, also turned so their back is what you see
EXACTLY ONE of each. No socks, no shoes, no ball, nothing else in the frame.

Everything carries over from image 1 unchanged: the same colours, the same fabric, the
same cut, the same collar, and above all the SAME PANELS AND
TRIM — a stripe, a panel or a piping that exists on the front continues around to the
back exactly as the garment's construction would carry it. Nothing is added that image 1
does not have, and nothing that image 1 has quietly disappears.

SLEEVES: this is the same garment as image 1, so it has exactly the same sleeves. If the
shirt in image 1 has short sleeves, this one has short sleeves and is NOT a sleeveless
vest or a tank top. If image 1 is sleeveless, this one is sleeveless. Look at image 1 and
copy what is there.

THE KIT — these are settled decisions, not suggestions. Do not substitute anything.
- shirt: Burnt orange short-sleeved baseball jersey with a full button placket and a plain fold-over collar. The club crest sits on the LEFT CHEST beside the placket, and the number 7 sits LOW on the front LEFT of the jersey near the hem, in cream-white — the collar, the placket, the crest, the numerals and every detail exactly as the athlete's own kit photograph shows them; copy them from the photograph and do not invent or adjust any of them. BACK (his own back is not visible in any photograph — this is a decision taken from the teammate jerseys visible behind him in photo2, which show the club's back number style): the number 7 large and centred across the shoulders in the same cream-white block style. No player name, no club name, no sponsor, no piping the photograph does not show, and no lettering of any kind. The navy training shirt in photo3 with a 12 on the sleeve is NOT the uniform — nothing from it appears on the jersey.
- shorts: Light grey full-length baseball pants, plain with no stripe and no piping, worn with a TAN-BROWN LEATHER belt with a plain metal buckle — the pants and the belt exactly as the kit photograph shows them.
- footwear: Light grey baseball cleats with white accents and a studded outsole, carrying the maker's white 'N' mark on the outer side — his own cleats exactly as photo3.png shows them, but CLEAN AND NEW in every shot: copy what he wears, never its condition. NOT sneakers.
- equipment: His MATCH cap — the burnt orange baseball cap with the cream club lark on the front, exactly as photo2.png shows it — worn in the hero, the pitch frame and the back frame. (The grey backwards cap in photo1 is everyday clothing, not part of the uniform, and never appears in the set.) A matte burnt orange BATTING HELMET, plain with no marks and no stickers, for the swing frame only — a deliberate plain team-colour decision, since no helmet of his is visible in the photographs. A plain white baseball with red stitching and a plain pale-wood bat with no lettering — also deliberate plain defaults, not visible in the photographs. The same cap, helmet, ball and bat in every shot.
- For socks the photographs did not
  answer, so use exactly this and nothing else:
a burnt orange baseball jersey with contrasting piping and a button placket, grey baseball pants with a burnt orange stripe, a burnt orange belt, and a burnt orange cap. The kit fits properly and is clean and well kept.
CONSISTENT ACROSS THE WHOLE SET — three of these frames sit side by side on one card, so
these must be identical in every shot and are not open to interpretation:
- Socks are burnt orange, matching the kit. Never white, never a different colour.
- Equipment: a plain white baseball with red stitching, and a plain wooden bat. The same one in every shot.
- Footwear: plain black baseball cleats with a studded outsole. NOT sneakers. The same pair in every shot, clean and unmarked.
- Where an item above is described from the athlete's own photographs, any manufacturer's
  logo it genuinely carries stays on it — that is their real clothing.
- socks came from the sport default, so
  this is PLAIN and UNBRANDED: no swoosh, no three
  stripes, no cat, no jumpman, no trefoil, no wordmark. Do not add a brand device to a
  garment nobody supplied.
- The club crest sits on the LEFT CHEST beside the button placket, about a hand's width across, exactly where and how large the kit photograph shows it. That position is settled and is the same in every frame.

THE BACK OF THE SHIRT carries the squad number 7, plus whatever else the
kit description above explicitly gives it — and nothing more. Add no mark the description
does not name.
NEVER any lettering: no club name, no player name, no sponsor, no word of any kind.
Nothing sits inside, on top of or overlapping the numerals — a badge, if the description
calls for one, is small, clear of the number, and the right way round.

Hard requirements:
- Everything is BRAND NEW and immaculate: no dirt, no scuffs, no wear, no sweat marks.
- Flat lay from directly overhead. No mannequin, no person, no body, no hanger, no rail.
- The same plain light grey surface and the same even lighting as image 1.
- No text of any kind beyond the number, no labels, no neck tag, no watermark.
- Sharp throughout, photographic, print quality. Square image.
